strategy.label: top-down model: monomer by mass balance, utility side from BAFU's own emulsion-polymerisation module, amounts calibrated within 0.5-2x of it
strategy.note: NOT S1. The cited report prints no inventory. The monomer is a mass balance (1 kg of PVC carries 1 kg of vinyl chloride; chain-growth polymerisation adds the monomer unchanged). The utility side - nitrogen blanketing, compressed air, process water, furnace gas, steam, electricity, auxiliary organics and the treatment of the unpolluted process water - is the input list of BAFU's own unit process 'Emulsion polymerisation, polyvinylchlorid' [RER], with its amounts as the centre of 0.5-2x bounds. Caveat, stated rather than hidden: that module is generic. Its one consumer in BAFU-2026 is 'Polyvinylalcohol, at plant' (1.94 kg of it), and its monomer slot is filled with 1.355 kg of dichloromethane, which is not a PVC reagent. Only its utility rows are used here; the monomer slot is replaced by vinyl chloride. That is why this is S3 with a template for the utilities, not S2.

technosphere.comment: Rajabihamedani 2025 sec. 3.6: 'For the implementation, the dataset "Chemical plant, organics {RER}U" is used. The quantity is the standard amount for production of chemicals of 4.0E-10 p.' The target carries exactly that, which is why 4.0E-10 is the upper bound here. It is the upper bound and not the amount because ESU added one chemical plant per *dataset*, i.e. one for a whole cradle-to-gate chain, while this model links to a precursor dataset that already carries its own 4.0E-10 - so a second one is a double count against the target's own convention. That matters more than its size suggests: of the 1790 flows in the cumulative vector of every one of these 14 datasets, 1316 get more than 90 % of their value from this single exchange (see scripts/plasticseurope_infrastructure_diagnostic.py), so doubling it doubles three quarters of the vector. The amount is therefore fitted between 0 and the report's 4.0E-10.

The dataset's own text names 'transportation of feedstock' but no report in the bundle gives a distance for it, so the amount is calibrated. The starting value is the ecoinvent v2 standard distance for precursor materials (Althaus 2007 sec. 34.6.7: 'As there is no information about the transport amounts, standard distances and means according to Frischknecht et al. (2007) are used for the different raw materials') = 0.6 tkm rail + 0.1 tkm lorry per kg of precursor, the ratio BAFU's Ethylene dichloride, Ethylene oxide, Ethyl benzene and PET-amorphous unit processes all carry; precursor mass here 1 kg. It is left free rather than fixed because the PlasticsEurope eco-profile accounts for its feedstock transport as elementary flows only - it carries no vehicle or track infrastructure - so an ecoinvent transport dataset adds a background the target cannot have, and the fit is the right place to decide how much of it belongs.

replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model from the dataset's own process description: styrene by mass balance, blowing agent and utilities calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. The cited report prints no inventory; what it says about EPS is an error correction (sec. 3.8, the rejected 28.5 kg of natural gas per kg). The input list here comes from the dataset's own ecoSpold technology field, which for EPS is unusually explicit and names, in order: styrene monomer, organic peroxide initiators, an aqueous phase, flame retardant and elemental carbon, suspension stabilisers, chain transfer agents, expanding aids, nucleating agents, plasticisers, pentane as the blowing agent, heating to 80-150 C, a centrifuge, drying and sieving, and a coating step. Amounts for none of them are printed anywhere in the bundle, so styrene is fixed by mass balance and everything else is fitted. The flame retardant and the elemental carbon of grey EPS are left out on purpose: no dataset is named for either and proposing one would be guessing - see gaps in the comment.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf (the dataset's own cited report)
evidence.note: Prints no unit-process inventory for any of its 14 datasets: 'All datasets addressed for the updates are nowadays only available as system processes and therefore are modelled accordingly in this study' (sec. 3.2); Foreground data = 'Cumulative inventories of Plastics as provided by PlasticsEurope' (Tab. 1.1). Verified page by page, including every table that is embedded as an image. The full finding is in specs/evidence/<code>/response-0-locate.json. What the report does give and is used here: sec. 3.6 (infrastructure, 4.0E-10 p of Chemical plant, organics).

evidence.source: bafu-2026 ecoSpold metadata of the target (technology)
evidence.note: 'Expandable Polystyrene (EPS) is produced by polymerisation of styrene monomer, a chain-growth reaction which is mostly initiated by free radical organic initiators. ... Styrene charged with organic peroxide initiators is added to an aqueous phase and forms a suspension upon stirring. Flame retardant and elemental carbon, as well as auxiliaries such as suspension stabilisers, chain transfer agents, expanding aids, nucleating agents and plasticisers can also be added. The styrene droplets polymerise to polystyrene during heating of the reactor between 80 and 150 C. Blowing agent, typically pentane, is added to the reactor during polymerisation and dissolves in the polymer, producing the Expandable Polystyrene bead. After the reactor is cooled, the polymer is separated from the water phase using a centrifuge. The EPS beads are dried and sieved into the required size fractions before being coated with additive'

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf
evidence.where: sec. 3.8 Obvious errors corrected in PE data
evidence.note: 'According to the latest PlasticsEurope data, methane emissions were first estimated for Polystyrene expandable seven times higher (0.226 kg vs. 0.031 kg) than previously estimated in UVEK 2025. This discrepancy is largely due to the significant consumption of natural gas - 28.5 kg - required to produce just 1 kg of polystyrene. Since such a high input is unrealistic a correction has been made.' A rejected figure, so it cannot be used as an amount; it is recorded because it is the only process-energy number the report ever prints for this dataset, and because it means the published vector for EPS carries a hand-made correction of unstated size.

nodes.name: Polystyrene, expandable, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Polystyrene, expandable, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: Suspension polymerisation of styrene with a pentane blowing agent, per kg of EPS beads. Gaps: the flame retardant, the elemental carbon of grey EPS (4 of the 14 plants behind the eco-profile), the peroxide initiator and the bead coating are named by the dataset and modelled only through the generic 'Chemicals organic, at plant'. Note also that the target carries 1.435 kg of 'Disposal, salt tailings potash mining, 0% water, to residual material landfill {CH}' per kg of EPS. Tab. 3.1 of the cited report (p. 11 of the PDF, the continuation page that pdftotext returns empty because the table is an image) shows where that comes from: 'tailings (deposited)', 'Overburden (deposited)' and 'Waste salt from KCl-production (wfr)' are all mapped to that one potash-tailings *treatment* dataset. Mining overburden routed through a waste-treatment chain is what gives the EPS target its three largest kilogram flows - 30.6 kg of waste water to river, 18.3 kg of air and 1.44 kg of basalt per kg of polystyrene - and it is why this dataset's kg-mass and top-50 scores cannot be met by any model of the polymerisation. Nothing in this model reproduces it, and nothing should. The waste-treatment services that the BAFU dataset already carries as explicit exchanges (Tab. 3.1 of Rajabihamedani 2025 documents how they were re-linked, but prints no amounts) are deliberately NOT part of this model: they were never collapsed away, so reconstructing them adds nothing, and copying their amounts out of the target would be reading the answer. strategy.label: top-down model: monomer by mass balance, input list from the dataset's own process description, energy calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. The cited report prints no inventory. The input list is the one the BAFU dataset itself declares in its ecoSpold technology/includedProcesses field, and the monomer amount is a mass balance, not a measurement: addition (chain-growth) polymerisation adds the monomer to the chain unchanged, so the repeat unit and the monomer have the same empirical formula and 1 kg of polymer needs 1 kg of monomer plus whatever is lost. No loss figure exists anywhere in the bundle, so 1.000 kg is used and the real value can only be higher - this is the one place where the model is knowingly at a bound. Electricity and steam are named by the dataset and quantified nowhere, so they are fitted, unbounded; they are the whole gate-to-gate difference between the polymer and its monomer. 'Propylene, at plant [RER]' is not one of the 101, so the harness does not flag it, but it is not a transparent unit process either: it carries 8 technosphere exchanges, all of them waste-treatment services, and 143 elementary flows - the same APME/PlasticsEurope shape as the datasets being rebuilt here. The chain therefore still terminates on aggregated data one level down, and saying so is part of the result.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf (the dataset's own cited report)
evidence.note: Prints no unit-process inventory for any of its 14 datasets: 'All datasets addressed for the updates are nowadays only available as system processes and therefore are modelled accordingly in this study' (sec. 3.2); Foreground data = 'Cumulative inventories of Plastics as provided by PlasticsEurope' (Tab. 1.1). Verified page by page, including every table that is embedded as an image. The full finding is in specs/evidence/<code>/response-0-locate.json. What the report does give and is used here: sec. 3.6 (infrastructure, 4.0E-10 p of Chemical plant, organics).

replaces.name: Polyvinylchloride, suspension polymerised, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: monomer by mass balance, input list from the dataset's own process description, energy calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. The cited report prints no inventory. The input list is the one the BAFU dataset itself declares in its ecoSpold technology/includedProcesses field, and the monomer amount is a mass balance, not a measurement: addition (chain-growth) polymerisation adds the monomer to the chain unchanged, so the repeat unit and the monomer have the same empirical formula and 1 kg of polymer needs 1 kg of monomer plus whatever is lost. No loss figure exists anywhere in the bundle, so 1.000 kg is used and the real value can only be higher - this is the one place where the model is knowingly at a bound. Electricity and steam are named by the dataset and quantified nowhere, so they are fitted, unbounded; they are the whole gate-to-gate difference between the polymer and its monomer. Suspension polymerisation is carried out in an aqueous phase with a suspension stabiliser, and both the water and the stabiliser are gaps here: the dataset's own text names neither, and nothing in the bundle quantifies them. Only the monomer, the energy and the transport are modelled. Re-point the monomer to 99a93e93-...-disagg with the input's `sandbox` field to chain this onto the VCM rebuild.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf (the dataset's own cited report)
evidence.note: Prints no unit-process inventory for any of its 14 datasets: 'All datasets addressed for the updates are nowadays only available as system processes and therefore are modelled accordingly in this study' (sec. 3.2); Foreground data = 'Cumulative inventories of Plastics as provided by PlasticsEurope' (Tab. 1.1). Verified page by page, including every table that is embedded as an image. The full finding is in specs/evidence/<code>/response-0-locate.json. What the report does give and is used here: sec. 3.6 (infrastructure, 4.0E-10 p of Chemical plant, organics).

evidence.source: bafu-2026 ecoSpold metadata of the target (includedProcesses / technology)
evidence.note: 'The polymerisation process, upstream processes like ethylene, chlorine, and VCM production, electricity, and steam production as well as transportation of feedstock and waste treatment.'

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf
evidence.where: Tab. 5.3 (cross-check only, not used for any amount)
evidence.note: Cumulative energy demand, this study: S-PVC 54.49 MJ/kg against Vinyl chloride 49.71 MJ/kg - about 4.8 MJ/kg for the suspension polymerisation step, 9 % of the total. Quoted as a sanity check on the fitted electricity and steam, and deliberately not used to set or bound them: it is an impact result, and no impact assessment enters this pipeline.

nodes.name: Polyvinylchloride, suspension polymerised, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Polyvinylchloride, suspension polymerised, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: Polymerisation step, per kg of granulate. The waste-treatment services that the BAFU dataset already carries as explicit exchanges (Tab. 3.1 of Rajabihamedani 2025 documents how they were re-linked, but prints no amounts) are deliberately NOT part of this model: they were never collapsed away, so reconstructing them adds nothing, and copying their amounts out of the target would be reading the answer. Adding the whole Tab. 3.1 candidate list as free inputs was tested on Ethylene glycol - the fit drove all eleven to ~1e-12 and the agreement did not move by a single flow - so they are left out. Consequence for the harness number: the target's cumulative vector gets its long tail of trace flows from those disposal chains, while this model gets a different tail from the ecoinvent-v2 chains of its own inputs; the two tails cannot agree, which caps the 'share of all flows within 10 %' far below what the main flows achieve. This model terminates on Vinyl chloride, at plant [RER], which is itself an ecoSpold type=2 dataset - the harness flags that, correctly. It is linked to the BAFU dataset rather than to the sibling rebuild so that this spec's check measures only this spec's evidence; re-point it with the input's `sandbox` field to chain the rebuilds together.

technosphere.comment: mass balance of chain-growth polymerisation: the repeat unit is the monomer, so 1 kg of polymer carries 1 kg of monomer; no conversion-loss figure is printed in any report of the bundle, so this is a lower bound, fixed (not fitted)

technosphere.comment: Rajabihamedani 2025 sec. 3.6: 'For the implementation, the dataset "Chemical plant, organics {RER}U" is used. The quantity is the standard amount for production of chemicals of 4.0E-10 p.' The target carries exactly that, which is why 4.0E-10 is the upper bound here. It is the upper bound and not the amount because ESU added one chemical plant per *dataset*, i.e. one for a whole cradle-to-gate chain, while this model links to a precursor dataset that already carries its own 4.0E-10 - so a second one is a double count against the target's own convention. That matters more than its size suggests: of the 1790 flows in the cumulative vector of every one of these 14 datasets, 1316 get more than 90 % of their value from this single exchange (see scripts/plasticseurope_infrastructure_diagnostic.py), so doubling it doubles three quarters of the vector. The amount is therefore fitted between 0 and the report's 4.0E-10.

The dataset's own text names 'transportation of feedstock' but no report in the bundle gives a distance for it, so the amount is calibrated. The starting value is the ecoinvent v2 standard distance for precursor materials (Althaus 2007 sec. 34.6.7: 'As there is no information about the transport amounts, standard distances and means according to Frischknecht et al. (2007) are used for the different raw materials') = 0.6 tkm rail + 0.1 tkm lorry per kg of precursor, the ratio BAFU's Ethylene dichloride, Ethylene oxide, Ethyl benzene and PET-amorphous unit processes all carry; precursor mass here 1 kg. It is left free rather than fixed because the PlasticsEurope eco-profile accounts for its feedstock transport as elementary flows only - it carries no vehicle or track infrastructure - so an ecoinvent transport dataset adds a background the target cannot have, and the fit is the right place to decide how much of it belongs.

replaces.name: Ethylene glycol, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: vintage transfer: the ecoinvent v2 unit process of the same product, transcribed from its report table and verified against the two co-products BAFU still carries
strategy.note: The cited report (Rajabihamedani 2025) prints no unit process - it documents only the post-processing of a PlasticsEurope system process (see specs/evidence/582ad303-.../response-0-locate.json). The inventory here is transcribed from Althaus 2007, ecoinvent report No. 8, Tab. 35.3, which documents the multi-output process 'ethylene oxide, in ethylene glycol plant' that ecoinvent v2 used for this same dataset name, and allocated to MEG with the report's own 85 % price-times-mass factor over its 0.825 kg of MEG. The transcription is verified, not assumed: applying the same table with the DEG factor (7 %/0.1 kg) and the TEG factor (8 %/0.04 kg) reproduces BAFU's own 'Diethylene glycol, at plant' and 'Triethylene glycol, at plant' unit processes on all eleven exchanges the table covers - exactly on nine of them (ethylene oxide 0.4921 kg, electricity 0.2639 kWh, chemical plant 2.8E-10, waste heat 0.945 MJ, acetaldehyde 9.8E-07, ethylene 4.2E-06, water 0.0042 m3, and the TEG column 1.406 / 0.754 / 8E-10) and to 0.15 % on the two four-digit ones (COD/BOD 2.013E-04 against 2.016E-04, TOC/DOC 5.248E-05 against 5.250E-05). The twelfth exchange, the waterborne water emission, is not in Tab. 35.3 at all and is taken from the co-products' own 0.95 ratio. This is S2 and not S1 because the BAFU dataset being rebuilt is the PlasticsEurope 2019 eco-profile (reference year 2023), a different data generation from the 1997-2000 ecoinvent v2 inventory transcribed here; the structure is the same product's, the vintage is not. Steam is calibrated because Tab. 35.3 omits it and sec. 35.6.2 says so explicitly, and the infrastructure is calibrated between 0 and the transcribed 4.1212E-10 because the ethylene-oxide precursor already carries one chemical plant of its own.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.where: Tab. 35.3 (printed p. 307, PDF p. 388), ch. 35 Ethylene Glycol
evidence.note: Multi-output process 'ethylene oxide, in ethylene glycol plant' [RER], per 1 kg: ethylene oxide, at plant 7.03E-1 kg; electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid 3.77E-1 kWh; chemical plant, organics 4.00E-10 unit; Water, unspecified natural origin 6.00E-03 m3; Heat, waste 1.35E+00 MJ; Acetaldehyde 1.40E-06 kg; Ethene 6.00E-06 kg; BOD5 2.88E-04 kg; COD 2.88E-01 kg (see note below); DOC 7.50E-05 kg; TOC 7.50E-05 kg. Outputs diethylene glycol 0.1 kg, ethylene glycol 0.825 kg, triethylene glycol 0.04 kg, with the allocation row 7 / 85 / 8 %. Every amount below is that column times 0.85/0.825 = 1.030303.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.note: 'It is assumed that an average 82.5% of the glycols consists of MEG. This report assumes that a further 10% is DEG, the remainder being TEG and heavy glycols.' Tab. 35.2 gives Input: Ethylene oxide 703, Output: MEG 825, DEG 100, TEG 40, Heavy glycols 35 (kg), with price x mass allocation factors 85 / 7 / 8 %. Sec. 35.5 notes the wider IPPC range: 'the glycol products typically consists of 70 - 95% w/w of MEG' - the 82.5 % split is one point in it.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.note: 'It must be assumed that some steam is utilized for glycol distillation. No figures are given. Electrical energy consumption is given as 0.377 kWh / kg in (BUWAL 232).' The steam input is therefore in the model but calibrated, unbounded - the report names it and refuses to quantify it.

evidence.source: bafu-2026: Diethylene glycol, at plant [RER] and Triethylene glycol, at plant [RER]
evidence.note: Both are 3-input unit processes still in BAFU-2026 and are the co-products of the very table transcribed here. Tab. 35.3 x 0.07/0.1 gives ethylene oxide 0.4921 kg, electricity 0.2639 kWh, chemical plant 2.80E-10 unit, water 0.0042 m3, waste heat 0.945 MJ, acetaldehyde 9.8E-07, ethylene 4.2E-06, BOD 2.016E-04, COD 2.016E-04, DOC/TOC 5.25E-05 - which is exactly what BAFU's DEG carries (0.4921 / 0.2639 / 2.8E-10 / 0.0042 / 0.945 / 9.8E-07 / 4.2E-06 / 2.013E-04 / 2.013E-04 / 5.248E-05). Same for TEG at 0.08/0.04 (EO 1.406, electricity 0.754, plant 8E-10). Two consequences: the transcription is verified, and the report's COD of 2.88E-01 kg is a typo for 2.88E-04 (the co-products carry BOD = COD), which is what is used here. The co-products also fix the water balance, 0.00399/0.0042 = 0.95 of the water input leaving as a waterborne emission; Tab. 35.3 gives only the input.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf
evidence.note: 'For all datasets, the inventory regarding infrastructure contributions was checked and supplemented. For the implementation, the dataset "Chemical plant, organics {RER}U" is used. The quantity is the standard amount for production of chemicals of 4.0E-10 p.' The BAFU target indeed carries 4.0E-10 p, and Tab. 35.3 gives the same 4.00E-10 unit - the two vintages agree on this one input.

The waste-treatment services and the infrastructure that BAFU's own aggregated dataset already carries explicitly are deliberately NOT copied into this model except for the infrastructure the report states; the point of the rebuild is the production chain, which is the part that was collapsed away.

replaces.name: Polyethylene, HDPE, granulate, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: monomer by mass balance, input list from the dataset's own process description, energy calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. The cited report prints no inventory. The input list is the one the BAFU dataset itself declares in its ecoSpold technology/includedProcesses field, and the monomer amount is a mass balance, not a measurement: addition (chain-growth) polymerisation adds the monomer to the chain unchanged, so the repeat unit and the monomer have the same empirical formula and 1 kg of polymer needs 1 kg of monomer plus whatever is lost. No loss figure exists anywhere in the bundle, so 1.000 kg is used and the real value can only be higher - this is the one place where the model is knowingly at a bound. Electricity and steam are named by the dataset and quantified nowhere, so they are fitted, unbounded; they are the whole gate-to-gate difference between the polymer and its monomer. HDPE is made by low-pressure catalytic polymerisation, LDPE by the high-pressure radical route and LLDPE by low-pressure copolymerisation with an alpha-olefin. The bundle documents none of that quantitatively, so the three specs differ only in what the fit puts into electricity and steam. The alpha-olefin comonomer of LLDPE (a few per cent of 1-butene/1-hexene) is a known gap: no dataset for it is named anywhere and folding it into the ethylene is the standard simplification.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf (the dataset's own cited report)
evidence.note: Prints no unit-process inventory for any of its 14 datasets: 'All datasets addressed for the updates are nowadays only available as system processes and therefore are modelled accordingly in this study' (sec. 3.2); Foreground data = 'Cumulative inventories of Plastics as provided by PlasticsEurope' (Tab. 1.1). Verified page by page, including every table that is embedded as an image. The full finding is in specs/evidence/<code>/response-0-locate.json. What the report does give and is used here: sec. 3.6 (infrastructure, 4.0E-10 p of Chemical plant, organics).

evidence.source: bafu-2026 ecoSpold metadata of the target (includedProcesses / technology)
evidence.note: 'The polymer process, upstream processes like ethylene production, electricity, and steam production as well as transportation of feedstock and waste treatment.' - the whole input list the dataset declares.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf
evidence.where: Tab. 5.3 (cross-check only, not used for any amount)
evidence.note: Cumulative energy demand, this study: HDPE 77.38 MJ/kg against Ethylene, average 70.73 MJ/kg, so the whole gate-to-gate step the fit has to find is worth about 6.7 MJ/kg, under 9 % of the total. Quoted as a sanity check on the fitted electricity and steam, and deliberately not used to set or bound them: it is an impact result, and no impact assessment enters this pipeline.

nodes.name: Polyethylene, HDPE, granulate, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Polyethylene, HDPE, granulate, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: Polymerisation step, per kg of granulate. The waste-treatment services that the BAFU dataset already carries as explicit exchanges (Tab. 3.1 of Rajabihamedani 2025 documents how they were re-linked, but prints no amounts) are deliberately NOT part of this model: they were never collapsed away, so reconstructing them adds nothing, and copying their amounts out of the target would be reading the answer. Adding the whole Tab. 3.1 candidate list as free inputs was tested on Ethylene glycol - the fit drove all eleven to ~1e-12 and the agreement did not move by a single flow - so they are left out. Consequence for the harness number: the target's cumulative vector gets its long tail of trace flows from those disposal chains, while this model gets a different tail from the ecoinvent-v2 chains of its own inputs; the two tails cannot agree, which caps the 'share of all flows within 10 %' far below what the main flows achieve. This model terminates on Ethylene, average, at plant [RER], which is itself an ecoSpold type=2 dataset - the harness flags that, correctly. It is linked to the BAFU dataset rather than to the sibling rebuild so that this spec's check measures only this spec's evidence; re-point it with the input's `sandbox` field to chain the rebuilds together.

technosphere.comment: mass balance of chain-growth polymerisation: the repeat unit is the monomer, so 1 kg of polymer carries 1 kg of monomer; no conversion-loss figure is printed in any report of the bundle, so this is a lower bound, fixed (not fitted)

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Electricity, medium voltage, production ENTSO-E, at grid
technosphere.comment: named by the dataset ('electricity ... production'), quantified nowhere in the bundle -> calibrated, unbounded
technosphere.supplier_name: Electricity, medium voltage, production ENTSO-E, at grid

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Steam, for chemical processes, at plant
technosphere.comment: named by the dataset ('steam production'), quantified nowhere in the bundle -> calibrated, unbounded
technosphere.supplier_name: Steam, for chemical processes, at plant

technosphere.comment: Rajabihamedani 2025 sec. 3.6: 'For the implementation, the dataset "Chemical plant, organics {RER}U" is used. The quantity is the standard amount for production of chemicals of 4.0E-10 p.' The target carries exactly that, which is why 4.0E-10 is the upper bound here. It is the upper bound and not the amount because ESU added one chemical plant per *dataset*, i.e. one for a whole cradle-to-gate chain, while this model links to a precursor dataset that already carries its own 4.0E-10 - so a second one is a double count against the target's own convention. That matters more than its size suggests: of the 1790 flows in the cumulative vector of every one of these 14 datasets, 1316 get more than 90 % of their value from this single exchange (see scripts/plasticseurope_infrastructure_diagnostic.py), so doubling it doubles three quarters of the vector. The amount is therefore fitted between 0 and the report's 4.0E-10.

The dataset's own text names 'transportation of feedstock' but no report in the bundle gives a distance for it, so the amount is calibrated. The starting value is the ecoinvent v2 standard distance for precursor materials (Althaus 2007 sec. 34.6.7: 'As there is no information about the transport amounts, standard distances and means according to Frischknecht et al. (2007) are used for the different raw materials') = 0.6 tkm rail + 0.1 tkm lorry per kg of precursor, the ratio BAFU's Ethylene dichloride, Ethylene oxide, Ethyl benzene and PET-amorphous unit processes all carry; precursor mass here 1 kg. It is left free rather than fixed because the PlasticsEurope eco-profile accounts for its feedstock transport as elementary flows only - it carries no vehicle or track infrastructure - so an ecoinvent transport dataset adds a background the target cannot have, and the fit is the right place to decide how much of it belongs.

replaces.name: Vinyl chloride, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: the balanced VCM process, input list from the dataset's own process description, amounts from the reaction stoichiometry, energy calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. The cited report prints no inventory (see the evidence block). The input list is the one the BAFU dataset itself states - 'The VCM production process, upstream processes like ethylene and chlorine production, electricity, and steam production as well as transportation of feedstock and waste treatment' - and the two material amounts follow from the balanced-process equations printed in Althaus 2007 sec. 34.5.3 with the yields of sec. 34.5.1. Electricity and steam are named by the dataset and quantified nowhere in the bundle, so they are fitted, unbounded. No direct process emissions are modelled: the only VCM emission factors in the bundle (Althaus Tab. 34.1) are for EDC, not for the cracking step.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf (the dataset's own cited report)
evidence.note: Prints no unit-process inventory for any of its 14 datasets: 'All datasets addressed for the updates are nowadays only available as system processes and therefore are modelled accordingly in this study' (sec. 3.2); Foreground data = 'Cumulative inventories of Plastics as provided by PlasticsEurope' (Tab. 1.1). Verified page by page, including every table that is embedded as an image. The full finding is in specs/evidence/<code>/response-0-locate.json. What the report does give and is used here: sec. 3.6 (infrastructure, 4.0E-10 p of Chemical plant, organics).

evidence.source: bafu-2026 ecoSpold metadata of the target (includedProcesses / technology)
evidence.note: 'The VCM production process, upstream processes like ethylene and chlorine production, electricity, and steam production as well as transportation of feedstock and waste treatment.' - this is the whole input list the dataset declares, and it is what the model contains.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.note: 'C2H4 + Cl2 -> C2H4Cl2 (Chlorination of ethylene to EDC) / C2H4Cl -> CH2CHCl + HCl (Cracking of EDC to form VCM) / C2H4 + 1/2 O2 + 2HCl -> C2H4Cl2 + H2O (Oxychlorination route to EDC)'. 'Often all the HCl generated in the cracking section is reused in producing EDC by oxychlorination. Plants that exhibit this characteristic and also do not export EDC are called “balanced”. The balanced process is the common process used as a Best Available Technology benchmark.' Summing the three gives the balanced overall reaction 2 C2H4 + Cl2 + 1/2 O2 -> 2 C2H3Cl + H2O, in which the HCl cancels - which is why VCM is modelled here from ethylene and chlorine directly and not from 1.583 kg of EDC (that route would double-count the chlorine, because half of it comes back as HCl).

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.where: sec. 34.5.1 EDC by direct chlorination of ethylene
evidence.note: 'Yield on ethylene 96-98% / on chlorine 98%' - the midpoint 97 % and the 98 % are applied to the stoichiometric amounts.

evidence.source: bafu-2026: Ethylene dichloride, at plant [RER]
evidence.note: The one BAFU unit process for the same chemistry carries 0.6 tkm rail + 0.1 tkm lorry per kg, chlorine, liquid, production mix 0.735 kg and ethylene 0.295 kg - it reproduces Althaus Tab. 34.3 exactly, which is the check that this way of reading the report gives back the dataset it built.

nodes.name: Vinyl chloride, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Vinyl chloride, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: Balanced EDC/VCM process, per kg of vinyl chloride monomer. The waste-treatment services that the BAFU dataset already carries as explicit exchanges (Tab. 3.1 of Rajabihamedani 2025 documents how they were re-linked, but prints no amounts) are deliberately NOT part of this model: they were never collapsed away, so reconstructing them adds nothing, and copying their amounts out of the target would be reading the answer. Adding the whole Tab. 3.1 candidate list as free inputs was tested on Ethylene glycol - the fit drove all eleven to ~1e-12 and the agreement did not move by a single flow - so they are left out. Consequence for the harness number: the target's cumulative vector gets its long tail of trace flows from those disposal chains, while this model gets a different tail from the ecoinvent-v2 chains of its own inputs; the two tails cannot agree, which caps the 'share of all flows within 10 %' far below what the main flows achieve. This model terminates on Ethylene, average, at plant [RER], which is itself an ecoSpold type=2 dataset - the harness flags that, correctly. It is linked to the BAFU dataset rather than to the sibling rebuild so that this spec's check measures only this spec's evidence; re-point it with the input's `sandbox` field to chain the rebuilds together.

technosphere.comment: balanced reaction 2 C2H4 + Cl2 + 1/2 O2 -> 2 C2H3Cl + H2O: M(C2H4)/M(C2H3Cl) = 28.054/62.498 = 0.4489 kg, / 0.97 yield on ethylene (Althaus sec. 34.5.1) = 0.4628 kg

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Chlorine, liquid, production mix, at plant
technosphere.comment: same reaction: 0.5*M(Cl2)/M(C2H3Cl) = 35.453/62.498 = 0.5672 kg, / 0.98 yield on chlorine (Althaus sec. 34.5.1) = 0.5788 kg; the dataset BAFU's own Ethylene dichloride unit process uses

technosphere.supplier_name: Electricity, medium voltage, production ENTSO-E, at grid

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Steam, for chemical processes, at plant
technosphere.comment: named by the dataset ('steam production'), quantified nowhere in the bundle -> calibrated, unbounded; EDC cracking to VCM is strongly endothermic
technosphere.supplier_name: Steam, for chemical processes, at plant

technosphere.comment: Rajabihamedani 2025 sec. 3.6: 'For the implementation, the dataset "Chemical plant, organics {RER}U" is used. The quantity is the standard amount for production of chemicals of 4.0E-10 p.' The target carries exactly that, which is why 4.0E-10 is the upper bound here. It is the upper bound and not the amount because ESU added one chemical plant per *dataset*, i.e. one for a whole cradle-to-gate chain, while this model links to a precursor dataset that already carries its own 4.0E-10 - so a second one is a double count against the target's own convention. That matters more than its size suggests: of the 1790 flows in the cumulative vector of every one of these 14 datasets, 1316 get more than 90 % of their value from this single exchange (see scripts/plasticseurope_infrastructure_diagnostic.py), so doubling it doubles three quarters of the vector. The amount is therefore fitted between 0 and the report's 4.0E-10.

The dataset's own text names 'transportation of feedstock' but no report in the bundle gives a distance for it, so the amount is calibrated. The starting value is the ecoinvent v2 standard distance for precursor materials (Althaus 2007 sec. 34.6.7: 'As there is no information about the transport amounts, standard distances and means according to Frischknecht et al. (2007) are used for the different raw materials') = 0.6 tkm rail + 0.1 tkm lorry per kg of precursor, the ratio BAFU's Ethylene dichloride, Ethylene oxide, Ethyl benzene and PET-amorphous unit processes all carry; precursor mass here 1.042 kg. It is left free rather than fixed because the PlasticsEurope eco-profile accounts for its feedstock transport as elementary flows only - it carries no vehicle or track infrastructure - so an ecoinvent transport dataset adds a background the target cannot have, and the fit is the right place to decide how much of it belongs.

replaces.name: Xylene, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: BREF ranges for a reformate xylene plant, feedstock split from the dataset's own text, every free amount bounded by a printed range
strategy.note: NOT S1. The cited report prints no inventory. Althaus 2007 ch. 96 is about this very dataset name, but its inventory tables 96.5-96.7 are the *cumulative* vector of the PlasticsEurope module - the report says so: 'Due to the fact that this dataset is cumulated it was not possible to use the other processes modelled in ecoinvent to obtain a transparent process chain' - so they are the aggregate this project is trying to open, not a unit process. What ch. 96 does print, from the EU BREF (European Commission 2002), is a gate-to-gate picture of a reformate xylene plant as ranges: Tab. 96.1 consumptions and yields, Tab. 96.2 air emissions, Tab. 96.3 wastewater, Tab. 96.4 solid wastes. That is what is modelled here. Every free amount carries bounds taken straight from those printed ranges - none of them was chosen to make the agreement look better, and the feedstock bounds in particular are very wide (1.37-4.35 kg per kg) because the printed yield range is. Same caveat as Althaus's own: 'Within the module assessed here there are only the resources and emissions considered which are given in the data source. Therefore no land use could be included and no direct soil emissions within the process chain are stated.'

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf (the dataset's own cited report)
evidence.note: Prints no unit-process inventory for any of its 14 datasets: 'All datasets addressed for the updates are nowadays only available as system processes and therefore are modelled accordingly in this study' (sec. 3.2); Foreground data = 'Cumulative inventories of Plastics as provided by PlasticsEurope' (Tab. 1.1). Verified page by page, including every table that is embedded as an image. The full finding is in specs/evidence/<code>/response-0-locate.json. What the report does give and is used here: sec. 3.6 (infrastructure, 4.0E-10 p of Chemical plant, organics).

evidence.source: bafu-2026 ecoSpold metadata of the target (technology)
evidence.note: 'Xylenes are commercially produced based on two different feedstocks: - Pyrolysis gasoline, a side product of thermal cracking (steam cracking) of hydrocarbons (e.g. naphtha, gas oil, ethane, propane, butanes, natural gas liquids) - Reformate, a product of catalytic reforming of naphtha. ... In Europe (EU27) xylenes are mainly produced via pyrolysis gasoline (14 %) and reformate (86 %).' The 14/86 split is the only quantitative statement about this dataset anywhere, and it fixes the feedstock mix.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.note: 'Energy usage for and precursor materials for xylene production (European Commission (2002))', column 'Reformate plant', per ton of feedstock: Fuel gas 3 - 10 kg; Steam (tons) 0.5 - 1.5; Electricity (MWh) <0.07. Production (tons) per ton of feedstock: p-xylene 0.23 - 0.48; o-xylene 0 - 0.25. Summing the two product ranges gives 0.23 - 0.73 t of xylenes per t of feedstock, i.e. 1.370 - 4.348 kg of feedstock per kg of product, and every consumption range is multiplied by that to get a per-kg-of-product range.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.where: Tab. 96.2 and Tab. 96.3 (same page), row 'BTX from aromatic mixture (source: a single plant)'
evidence.note: Air, kg/ton product: Methane 0.086; SO2 0.53; Particulates 0.008 kg/ton *feedstock*; VOC 0.03 toluene and 0.2 NMVOCtot. Water, kg/ton product: Benzene 0.003; Toluene 0.001; COD 0.087; N-Kjeldahl 0.0009. Two rows are not used: the particulates, because they are per ton of feedstock and the feedstock amount here is itself calibrated, and the second 'Methane' column (0.09), because the table has two columns with that same header and the report gives no way to tell what the second one is. The caption reads 'Air emissions for toluene production' inside the xylenes chapter, which is a copy-paste slip in the report; the rows are the BTX plant the chapter is about.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.note: kg/ton product: Catalysts 0.05 'recycled via supplier'; Clay, desiccant material, inert balls 0.006 'reused after regeneration'; Activated carbon 0.01 'incinerated'; Filter cloth etc. 0.0009 'incinerated'. The first two leave the system as recovered material and are skipped; the two incinerated streams are modelled together, since 'The wastes are usually recycled, landfilled or incinerated in a hazardous waste incinerator.'

nodes.name: Xylene, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Xylene, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: Separation of mixed xylenes from reformate (86 %) and pyrolysis gasoline (14 %), per kg. Gaps: no reformate dataset exists in BAFU, so naphtha - the feed of the catalytic reformer - stands in for it and the reforming step itself is missing from the chain; particulate emissions are per ton of feedstock and cannot be fixed while the feedstock is calibrated; the isomer separation described in sec. 96.5.1 is not quantified anywhere. The waste-treatment services that the BAFU dataset already carries as explicit exchanges (Tab. 3.1 of Rajabihamedani 2025 documents how they were re-linked, but prints no amounts) are deliberately NOT part of this model: they were never collapsed away, so reconstructing them adds nothing, and copying their amounts out of the target would be reading the answer. Adding the whole Tab. 3.1 candidate list as free inputs was tested on Ethylene glycol - the fit drove all eleven to ~1e-12 and the agreement did not move by a single flow - so they are left out. Consequence for the harness number: the target's cumulative vector gets its long tail of trace flows from those disposal chains, while this model gets a different tail from the ecoinvent-v2 chains of its own inputs; the two tails cannot agree, which caps the 'share of all flows within 10 %' far below what the main flows achieve. This model terminates on Pyrolysis gasoline, production mix, at plant [RER], itself one of the 101 and the one dataset of this family that could not be rebuilt at all, which is itself an ecoSpold type=2 dataset - the harness flags that, correctly. It is linked to the BAFU dataset rather than to the sibling rebuild so that this spec's check measures only this spec's evidence; re-point it with the input's `sandbox` field to chain the rebuilds together.

technosphere.comment: reformate route, 86% of EU27 xylene (dataset text) x the feedstock range of Tab. 96.1 (1.370-4.348 kg feedstock per kg product) = 1.1781-3.7391 kg; naphtha stands in for reformate, which BAFU does not have

technosphere.comment: Rajabihamedani 2025 sec. 3.6: 'For the implementation, the dataset "Chemical plant, organics {RER}U" is used. The quantity is the standard amount for production of chemicals of 4.0E-10 p.' The target carries exactly that, which is why 4.0E-10 is the upper bound here. It is the upper bound and not the amount because ESU added one chemical plant per *dataset*, i.e. one for a whole cradle-to-gate chain, while this model links to a precursor dataset that already carries its own 4.0E-10 - so a second one is a double count against the target's own convention. That matters more than its size suggests: of the 1790 flows in the cumulative vector of every one of these 14 datasets, 1316 get more than 90 % of their value from this single exchange (see scripts/plasticseurope_infrastructure_diagnostic.py), so doubling it doubles three quarters of the vector. The amount is therefore fitted between 0 and the report's 4.0E-10.

datasets.bafu_name: Titanium dioxide, chloride process, at plant

replaces.name: Titanium dioxide, chloride process, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: transcription drafted from the report excerpt by the LLM pipeline (reverse-bafu draft)
strategy.note: basis: per 1 kg of TiO2; Tab. 85.3 is headed 'Kg per kg of product', Tab. 85.5 'Consumption per kg of product (MJ/kg)', Tab. 85.7 and Tab. 85.9 'Gram per kg of product'. The CHLORIDE-process column is used.; allocation: none stated for the TiO2 process itself. Review every derivation; unreviewed entries have reviewed_by = null.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.note: report sha256 68e0839ffea919f9…, text sha256 e1b3f9c29c3269b8…

gaps_reported_by_model: Section 85.6 says 'This inventory is based on confidential information provided by industry sources. The input information may not be divulged.' The printed BAT-Notes figures are what the report compares against, not necessarily the exact dataset amounts.
No transport, no infrastructure (chemical plant) and no water input are quantified anywhere in the excerpt for the TiO2 process; they are therefore not included.
Tab. 85.5 gives no coal for the chloride process and no breakdown of which fuel produces the steam beyond the sentence about a natural gas boiler.
The excerpt gives no process water, no NOx and no organic emissions for the chloride route.
skipped_items: Titanium dioxide, chloride process, at plant: product — Reference product; the whole excerpt is per kg of product.

nodes.name: Titanium dioxide, chloride process, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Titanium dioxide, chloride process, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: drafted from 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf pp. 845-847

technosphere.comment: Chloride-process precursor. The text adds 'The chloride process titanium dioxide is also assumed to stem from ilmenite, although in fact rutile, synthetic rutile and /or beneficiate are used. The data for mining of ilmenite are taken from (BUWAL 232).' so the supplying dataset is the ilmenite/rutile ore, not TiO2 itself.

provenance.quote: Synthetic rutile   ng   1.06   (Chemlink.com)   [Tab. 85.3 precursors for TiO2 production, chloride-process column, 'Kg per kg of product']
provenance.mapping_reason: Tab. 85.3 names 'Synthetic rutile' for the chloride route; the rutile concentrate is that material, while ilmenite is the lower-grade ore the sulfate route uses.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Chlorine, liquid, production mix, at plant
technosphere.comment: Printed value for the chloride process.
technosphere.supplier_name: Chlorine, liquid, production mix, at plant

provenance.quote: Chlorine   na   0.18   (UBA BAT Notes, 2001)   [Tab. 85.3 precursors for TiO2 production, chloride-process column]
provenance.mapping_reason: Exact substance and a production mix, as the report gives no specific electrolysis route; chlorine dioxide is a different chemical.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: xxx Electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid
technosphere.comment: 1.51 MJ (TiO2 manufacture) + 0.83 MJ (follow-up treatment) = 2.34 MJ/kg, the two columns of the same row. The text says the model facility 'imports UCTE grid electricity'.
technosphere.supplier_name: xxx Electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid

provenance.quote: Electric energy   1.51   0.83   [Tab. 85.5 energy consumption for TiO2 production (chloride process), TiO2 manufacture + Follow-up treatment]
provenance.factor_source: 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ, so MJ x 0.2778 = kWh (ecoinvent convention)
provenance.mapping_reason: The report says the model plant 'imports UCTE grid electricity'; this is the UCTE production mix, beating the single-fuel UCTE variants and the RER/CH grids.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Heat, natural gas, at industrial furnace 1MW
technosphere.comment: 1.7 + 7.7 = 9.4 MJ/kg. The text: 'The model facility portrayed here uses natural gas in a boiler to produce steam', so the steam is entered as natural-gas heat in MJ.
technosphere.supplier_name: Heat, natural gas, at industrial furnace 1MW

provenance.quote: Steam   1.7   7.7   [Tab. 85.5 energy consumption for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
provenance.mapping_reason: The report: 'uses natural gas in a boiler to produce steam'; this is delivered heat in MJ from a natural-gas furnace, which matches the MJ/kg the table gives, beating the 'burned in' variants that model the combustion itself.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Natural gas, burned in industrial furnace 1MW
technosphere.comment: 2.9 + 4.2 = 7.1 MJ/kg of direct process gas, separate from the gas burned for steam.
technosphere.supplier_name: Natural gas, burned in industrial furnace 1MW

provenance.quote: Gas   2.9   4.2   [Tab. 85.5 energy consumption for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
provenance.mapping_reason: Direct process gas burned on site, which is what the separate 'Gas' row of Tab. 85.5 is, as opposed to the gas that makes the steam.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: xx Disposal, residue from TiO2 prod. Cl, 56% water, to residual material landfill
technosphere.comment: 0.11 + 2.25 = 2.36 g/kg. Treated here as a disposal service (an input), since the report lists it under wastewater emissions but it is a solid residue. Low confidence on which disposal dataset applies.
technosphere.supplier_name: xx Disposal, residue from TiO2 prod. Cl, 56% water, to residual material landfill

provenance.quote: Filter residues   0.11   2.25   [Tab. 85.9 wastewater emissions for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: The disposal dataset made for exactly this residue stream of the chloride route, beating the SO4 variant and the generic residue landfills.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: xx Disposal, residue from TiO2 prod. Cl, 56% water, to residual material landfill
technosphere.comment: The excerpt gives 184 g/kg from the BAT notes and says industry suggests up to 1 kg/kg; entered as a bounded free input over exactly that printed range.
technosphere.supplier_name: xx Disposal, residue from TiO2 prod. Cl, 56% water, to residual material landfill

provenance.quote: Chloride process. According to (UBA BAT Notes, 2001), chloride process sludges total 184 g / kg product. Industry sources however suggest somewhat higher values, ranging up to 1 kg / kg product
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: Same stream as the filter residues and the only chloride-route TiO2 disposal dataset in the database.

biosphere.comment: 0.005 g (storage) + 0.186 g (follow-up treatment) = 0.191 g/kg. The report does not state a size fraction for the chloride route.

provenance.quote: Particles   0.005   ng   ng   0.186   [Tab. 85.7 direct air emissions for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: The only candidate; the report states no particle size fraction for TiO2, so the unspecified particulate flow is the honest choice.

biosphere.comment: The asterisk in the table marks 0.024 g/kg as the value the report actually uses for the model chloride plant.

provenance.quote: HCl   ng   0.007   0.024 *   ng   * This value is used for the model chloride plant.   [Tab. 85.7]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: Exact substance in the stated air compartment; the soil and water copies are the wrong compartment and 'Chloride' is the ion, not HCl.

biosphere.comment: Printed value.

provenance.quote: SO2   ng   ng   1.68   ng   [Tab. 85.7 direct air emissions for TiO2 production (chloride process), off-gas treatment]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: Exact substance and compartment; 'Sulfur Oxides' is the aggregate and 'Sulfur' the element.

biosphere.comment: The table prints 0.011 g/kg but the footnote below it states 'This report uses a value of 0.5 g iron per kg produced TiO2'; the footnote value is the one the dataset was built with.

provenance.quote: Iron   0.011 *   ng   ...   This report uses a value of 0.5 g iron per kg produced TiO2   [Tab. 85.9 wastewater emissions (chloride process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: The report says only 'Iron' with no oxidation state, so the unspecified iron flow beats Iron(2+) and Iron(3+).

biosphere.comment: Printed value.

provenance.quote: Cadmium   0.00000022   ng   [Tab. 85.9 wastewater emissions for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: Exact substance and compartment; Cadmium(2+) presumes an oxidation state the report does not give and Cadmium-109 is a radionuclide.

biosphere.comment: Printed value.

provenance.quote: Mercury   0.00000022   ng   [Tab. 85.9 wastewater emissions for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: Exact substance and compartment; Mercury(2+) presumes a speciation the report does not give.

strategy.label: transcription drafted from the report excerpt by the LLM pipeline (reverse-bafu draft)
strategy.note: basis: per 1 kg of wood preservative; the table's product row reads 'wood preservative, inorganic salt, containing Cr, at plant  1.00E+00 kg'; allocation: none stated; single-product process. Review every derivation; unreviewed entries have reviewed_by = null.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI wood as fuel and const. mat. - Werner.pdf
evidence.note: report sha256 1f2e06f8a69ca03e…, text sha256 207d840fb9d1bcd4…

gaps_reported_by_model: The five material amounts (boric acid, chromium oxide, copper oxide, UCTE electricity, tap water) are printed as 'confidential'. The excerpt gives no numbers for them at all; they are entered as free parameters with wide bounds and are determined by the calibration step, not by the report.
The report gives no process emissions for this dataset ('No process emission data are available' in the BAFU metadata); only the calculated waste heat is listed.

The bounds attached to the confidential rows are not from the report. They are deliberately wide search ranges (0.001-1 kg for the salts, since the product is 1 kg of mixed salts; 1e-4 to 5 kWh; 0.001-100 kg of water).

replaces.name: Purified terephthalic acid, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: p-xylene by the oxidation stoichiometry from the dataset's own process description, energy calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. The cited report prints no inventory and says of PTA only that a x1000 correction was applied to one land-occupation flow (sec. 3.8). The dataset's own includedProcesses field names the chemistry - 'Crude terephthalic acid (CTA) is produced by oxidation of p-xylene. A subsequent purification step leads to purified terephthalic acid (PTA)' - and the feedstock amount follows from that reaction. Two honest weaknesses: (1) the amount is the theoretical minimum, because no yield is printed anywhere in the bundle, so the model is low on p-xylene by whatever the real loss is; (2) BAFU has only 'Xylene, at plant', the mixed-isomer dataset, not p-xylene, so the isomer separation - which Althaus 2007 sec. 96.5.1 describes as crystallisation or molecular-sieve adsorption and does not quantify - is missing from the chain. The acetic acid solvent and the cobalt/manganese/bromide catalyst of the oxidation step are named by neither the dataset nor any report in the bundle and are left out rather than guessed.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf (the dataset's own cited report)
evidence.note: Prints no unit-process inventory for any of its 14 datasets: 'All datasets addressed for the updates are nowadays only available as system processes and therefore are modelled accordingly in this study' (sec. 3.2); Foreground data = 'Cumulative inventories of Plastics as provided by PlasticsEurope' (Tab. 1.1). Verified page by page, including every table that is embedded as an image. The full finding is in specs/evidence/<code>/response-0-locate.json. What the report does give and is used here: sec. 3.6 (infrastructure, 4.0E-10 p of Chemical plant, organics).

evidence.source: bafu-2026 ecoSpold metadata of the target (includedProcesses)
evidence.note: 'Crude terephthalic acid (CTA) is produced by oxidation of p-xylene. A subsequent purification step leads to purified terephthalic acid (PTA). In addition to these foreground processes, the following processes in the supply chain are considered for this EPD: extraction and refinery of crude oil and natural gas, steam cracking of hydrocarbons (predominantly naphtha) into lower olefins and pygas, catalytic reforming of naphtha, and the extraction and production of p-xylene from both pygas and reformate (xylene loop).'

evidence.source: stoichiometry of the p-xylene oxidation
evidence.note: C8H10 + 3 O2 -> C8H6O4 + 2 H2O. Per kg of PTA: M(C8H10)/M(C8H6O4) = 106.165/166.131 = 0.6390 kg of p-xylene. The oxygen is taken from air and is not an inventoried input, as in every air-oxidation process in BAFU (cf. Ethylene oxide, at plant, whose oxygen is a purchased pure-O2 input and is therefore listed there but not here).

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.note: Describes the isomer separation that this model cannot represent: 'Crystallization techniques take advantage of the spread of melting points ... p-Xylene can also be recovered using solid absorption of the molecular-sieve type.' No amounts are given for it anywhere.

nodes.name: Purified terephthalic acid, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Purified terephthalic acid, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: Air oxidation of p-xylene to CTA plus purification to PTA, per kg. The waste-treatment services that the BAFU dataset already carries as explicit exchanges (Tab. 3.1 of Rajabihamedani 2025 documents how they were re-linked, but prints no amounts) are deliberately NOT part of this model: they were never collapsed away, so reconstructing them adds nothing, and copying their amounts out of the target would be reading the answer. Adding the whole Tab. 3.1 candidate list as free inputs was tested on Ethylene glycol - the fit drove all eleven to ~1e-12 and the agreement did not move by a single flow - so they are left out. Consequence for the harness number: the target's cumulative vector gets its long tail of trace flows from those disposal chains, while this model gets a different tail from the ecoinvent-v2 chains of its own inputs; the two tails cannot agree, which caps the 'share of all flows within 10 %' far below what the main flows achieve. This model terminates on Xylene, at plant [RER], which is itself an ecoSpold type=2 dataset - the harness flags that, correctly. It is linked to the BAFU dataset rather than to the sibling rebuild so that this spec's check measures only this spec's evidence; re-point it with the input's `sandbox` field to chain the rebuilds together.

technosphere.comment: C8H10 + 3 O2 -> C8H6O4 + 2 H2O: 106.165/166.131 = 0.6390 kg, the theoretical minimum (no yield printed in the bundle); mixed xylene stands in for p-xylene, see the strategy note

technosphere.comment: Rajabihamedani 2025 sec. 3.6: 'For the implementation, the dataset "Chemical plant, organics {RER}U" is used. The quantity is the standard amount for production of chemicals of 4.0E-10 p.' The target carries exactly that, which is why 4.0E-10 is the upper bound here. It is the upper bound and not the amount because ESU added one chemical plant per *dataset*, i.e. one for a whole cradle-to-gate chain, while this model links to a precursor dataset that already carries its own 4.0E-10 - so a second one is a double count against the target's own convention. That matters more than its size suggests: of the 1790 flows in the cumulative vector of every one of these 14 datasets, 1316 get more than 90 % of their value from this single exchange (see scripts/plasticseurope_infrastructure_diagnostic.py), so doubling it doubles three quarters of the vector. The amount is therefore fitted between 0 and the report's 4.0E-10.

The dataset's own text names 'transportation of feedstock' but no report in the bundle gives a distance for it, so the amount is calibrated. The starting value is the ecoinvent v2 standard distance for precursor materials (Althaus 2007 sec. 34.6.7: 'As there is no information about the transport amounts, standard distances and means according to Frischknecht et al. (2007) are used for the different raw materials') = 0.6 tkm rail + 0.1 tkm lorry per kg of precursor, the ratio BAFU's Ethylene dichloride, Ethylene oxide, Ethyl benzene and PET-amorphous unit processes all carry; precursor mass here 0.639 kg. It is left free rather than fixed because the PlasticsEurope eco-profile accounts for its feedstock transport as elementary flows only - it carries no vehicle or track infrastructure - so an ecoinvent transport dataset adds a background the target cannot have, and the fit is the right place to decide how much of it belongs.

It is the upper bound and not the amount because ESU added one chemical plant per *dataset*, i.e. one for a whole cradle-to-gate chain, while this model links to a precursor dataset that already carries its own 4.0E-10 - so a second one is a double count against the target's own convention. That matters more than its size suggests: of the 1790 flows in the cumulative vector of every one of these 14 datasets, 1316 get more than 90 % of their value from this single exchange (see scripts/plasticseurope_infrastructure_diagnostic.py), so doubling it doubles three quarters of the vector. The amount is therefore fitted between 0 and the report's 4.0E-10.

The dataset's own text names 'transportation of feedstock' but no report in the bundle gives a distance for it, so the amount is calibrated. The starting value is the ecoinvent v2 standard distance for precursor materials (Althaus 2007 sec. 34.6.7: 'As there is no information about the transport amounts, standard distances and means according to Frischknecht et al. (2007) are used for the different raw materials') = 0.6 tkm rail + 0.1 tkm lorry per kg of precursor, the ratio BAFU's Ethylene dichloride, Ethylene oxide, Ethyl benzene and PET-amorphous unit processes all carry; precursor mass here 1 kg. It is left free rather than fixed because the PlasticsEurope eco-profile accounts for its feedstock transport as elementary flows only - it carries no vehicle or track infrastructure - so an ecoinvent transport dataset adds a background the target cannot have, and the fit is the right place to decide how much of it belongs.

datasets.bafu_name: Polyethylene terephthalate, granulate, bottle grade, at plant

replaces.name: Polyethylene terephthalate, granulate, bottle grade, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: template transfer from BAFU's own PET-granulate-amorphous unit process, the six energy inputs calibrated within 0.5-2x
strategy.note: The cited report prints no inventory. BAFU-2026 does carry a 16-input unit process for the same polymer in its other grade - 'Polyethylene terephthalate, granulate, amorphous, at plant' [RER] - and the target declares exactly that structure: 'The polymer process, upstream processes like pX, PTA, and MEG production, electricity, and steam production as well as transportation of feedstock and waste treatment.' Bottle grade differs from amorphous by a solid-state polycondensation step, which is extra heat and residence time and no extra material; the six energy inputs are therefore free within 0.5-2x of the template (the bound convention of the committed gypsum-fibre-board S2 spec) and the three material inputs are fixed. This is the best-evidenced of the family after ethylene glycol, and it is the only one of the fourteen whose direct process emissions are known at all - they come with the template.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf (the dataset's own cited report)
evidence.note: Prints no unit-process inventory for any of its 14 datasets: 'All datasets addressed for the updates are nowadays only available as system processes and therefore are modelled accordingly in this study' (sec. 3.2); Foreground data = 'Cumulative inventories of Plastics as provided by PlasticsEurope' (Tab. 1.1). Verified page by page, including every table that is embedded as an image. The full finding is in specs/evidence/<code>/response-0-locate.json. What the report does give and is used here: sec. 3.6 (infrastructure, 4.0E-10 p of Chemical plant, organics).

evidence.source: bafu-2026 ecoSpold metadata of the target (includedProcesses)
evidence.note: 'The polymer process, upstream processes like pX, PTA, and MEG production, electricity, and steam production as well as transportation of feedstock and waste treatment.'

evidence.source: bafu-2026: Polyethylene terephthalate, granulate, amorphous, at plant [RER] (unit process, 16 inputs, 15 direct flows)
evidence.note: Per kg: purified terephthalic acid 0.875 kg, ethylene glycol 0.334 kg, nitrogen liquid 0.0298 kg, steam 0.94 kg, electricity 0.194 kWh, heat natural gas 0.665 MJ, heat heavy fuel oil 0.494 MJ, heat hard coal 0.306 MJ, heat light fuel oil 0.165 MJ, chemical plant organics 4.0E-10 unit, transport rail 0.743 tkm + lorry 0.124 tkm, four disposal services, and 15 direct elementary flows. The four disposal services are dropped here: the bottle-grade target declares no waste-treatment exchanges at all (its only technosphere exchange is the 4.0E-10 chemical plant), so copying them in would add a chain the dataset does not have.

evidence.source: stoichiometry of the PET esterification
evidence.where: cross-check of the two material amounts
evidence.note: n HOOC-C6H4-COOH + n HO-C2H4-OH -> [-OC-C6H4-CO-O-C2H4-O-]n + 2n H2O. Per kg of repeat unit (M = 192.17): PTA 166.131/192.17 = 0.8645 kg, MEG 62.068/192.17 = 0.3230 kg. The template sits 1.2 % and 3.4 % above those minima, which is the expected order for process losses - the template is consistent with the chemistry, which is why both are kept fixed rather than fitted.

nodes.name: Polyethylene terephthalate, granulate, bottle grade, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Polyethylene terephthalate, granulate, bottle grade, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: Esterification/polycondensation of PTA and MEG plus the solid-state step, per kg of bottle-grade granulate. The waste-treatment services that the BAFU dataset already carries as explicit exchanges (Tab. 3.1 of Rajabihamedani 2025 documents how they were re-linked, but prints no amounts) are deliberately NOT part of this model: they were never collapsed away, so reconstructing them adds nothing, and copying their amounts out of the target would be reading the answer. Adding the whole Tab. 3.1 candidate list as free inputs was tested on Ethylene glycol - the fit drove all eleven to ~1e-12 and the agreement did not move by a single flow - so they are left out. Consequence for the harness number: the target's cumulative vector gets its long tail of trace flows from those disposal chains, while this model gets a different tail from the ecoinvent-v2 chains of its own inputs; the two tails cannot agree, which caps the 'share of all flows within 10 %' far below what the main flows achieve. This model terminates on Purified terephthalic acid, at plant [RER] and Ethylene glycol, at plant [RER], both of them among the 101, which is itself an ecoSpold type=2 dataset - the harness flags that, correctly. It is linked to the BAFU dataset rather than to the sibling rebuild so that this spec's check measures only this spec's evidence; re-point it with the input's `sandbox` field to chain the rebuilds together.

replaces.name: Polyethylene, LLDPE, granulate, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: monomer by mass balance, input list from the dataset's own process description, energy calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. The cited report prints no inventory. The input list is the one the BAFU dataset itself declares in its ecoSpold technology/includedProcesses field, and the monomer amount is a mass balance, not a measurement: addition (chain-growth) polymerisation adds the monomer to the chain unchanged, so the repeat unit and the monomer have the same empirical formula and 1 kg of polymer needs 1 kg of monomer plus whatever is lost. No loss figure exists anywhere in the bundle, so 1.000 kg is used and the real value can only be higher - this is the one place where the model is knowingly at a bound. Electricity and steam are named by the dataset and quantified nowhere, so they are fitted, unbounded; they are the whole gate-to-gate difference between the polymer and its monomer. The alpha-olefin comonomer (typically a few per cent of 1-butene or 1-hexene) is a gap: no comonomer is named in the dataset's own text and no dataset for one is identified, so it is carried inside the ethylene.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf (the dataset's own cited report)
evidence.note: Prints no unit-process inventory for any of its 14 datasets: 'All datasets addressed for the updates are nowadays only available as system processes and therefore are modelled accordingly in this study' (sec. 3.2); Foreground data = 'Cumulative inventories of Plastics as provided by PlasticsEurope' (Tab. 1.1). Verified page by page, including every table that is embedded as an image. The full finding is in specs/evidence/<code>/response-0-locate.json. What the report does give and is used here: sec. 3.6 (infrastructure, 4.0E-10 p of Chemical plant, organics).

evidence.source: bafu-2026 ecoSpold metadata of the target (includedProcesses / technology)
evidence.note: 'The polymer process, upstream processes like ethylene production, electricity, and steam production as well as transportation of feedstock and waste treatment.' - the whole input list the dataset declares.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf
evidence.where: Tab. 5.3 (cross-check only, not used for any amount)
evidence.note: Cumulative energy demand, this study: LLDPE 76.95 MJ/kg against Ethylene, average 70.73 MJ/kg - about 6.2 MJ/kg, 8 % of the total. Quoted as a sanity check on the fitted electricity and steam, and deliberately not used to set or bound them: it is an impact result, and no impact assessment enters this pipeline.

nodes.name: Polyethylene, LLDPE, granulate, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Polyethylene, LLDPE, granulate, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: Polymerisation step, per kg of granulate. The waste-treatment services that the BAFU dataset already carries as explicit exchanges (Tab. 3.1 of Rajabihamedani 2025 documents how they were re-linked, but prints no amounts) are deliberately NOT part of this model: they were never collapsed away, so reconstructing them adds nothing, and copying their amounts out of the target would be reading the answer. Adding the whole Tab. 3.1 candidate list as free inputs was tested on Ethylene glycol - the fit drove all eleven to ~1e-12 and the agreement did not move by a single flow - so they are left out. Consequence for the harness number: the target's cumulative vector gets its long tail of trace flows from those disposal chains, while this model gets a different tail from the ecoinvent-v2 chains of its own inputs; the two tails cannot agree, which caps the 'share of all flows within 10 %' far below what the main flows achieve. This model terminates on Ethylene, average, at plant [RER], which is itself an ecoSpold type=2 dataset - the harness flags that, correctly. It is linked to the BAFU dataset rather than to the sibling rebuild so that this spec's check measures only this spec's evidence; re-point it with the input's `sandbox` field to chain the rebuilds together.

technosphere.comment: mass balance of chain-growth polymerisation: the repeat unit is the monomer, so 1 kg of polymer carries 1 kg of monomer; no conversion-loss figure is printed in any report of the bundle, so this is a lower bound, fixed (not fitted)

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Electricity, medium voltage, production ENTSO-E, at grid
technosphere.comment: named by the dataset ('electricity ... production'), quantified nowhere in the bundle -> calibrated, unbounded
technosphere.supplier_name: Electricity, medium voltage, production ENTSO-E, at grid

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Steam, for chemical processes, at plant
technosphere.comment: named by the dataset ('steam production'), quantified nowhere in the bundle -> calibrated, unbounded
technosphere.supplier_name: Steam, for chemical processes, at plant

technosphere.comment: Rajabihamedani 2025 sec. 3.6: 'For the implementation, the dataset "Chemical plant, organics {RER}U" is used. The quantity is the standard amount for production of chemicals of 4.0E-10 p.' The target carries exactly that, which is why 4.0E-10 is the upper bound here. It is the upper bound and not the amount because ESU added one chemical plant per *dataset*, i.e. one for a whole cradle-to-gate chain, while this model links to a precursor dataset that already carries its own 4.0E-10 - so a second one is a double count against the target's own convention. That matters more than its size suggests: of the 1790 flows in the cumulative vector of every one of these 14 datasets, 1316 get more than 90 % of their value from this single exchange (see scripts/plasticseurope_infrastructure_diagnostic.py), so doubling it doubles three quarters of the vector. The amount is therefore fitted between 0 and the report's 4.0E-10.

The dataset's own text names 'transportation of feedstock' but no report in the bundle gives a distance for it, so the amount is calibrated. The starting value is the ecoinvent v2 standard distance for precursor materials (Althaus 2007 sec. 34.6.7: 'As there is no information about the transport amounts, standard distances and means according to Frischknecht et al. (2007) are used for the different raw materials') = 0.6 tkm rail + 0.1 tkm lorry per kg of precursor, the ratio BAFU's Ethylene dichloride, Ethylene oxide, Ethyl benzene and PET-amorphous unit processes all carry; precursor mass here 1 kg. It is left free rather than fixed because the PlasticsEurope eco-profile accounts for its feedstock transport as elementary flows only - it carries no vehicle or track infrastructure - so an ecoinvent transport dataset adds a background the target cannot have, and the fit is the right place to decide how much of it belongs.

strategy.label: transcription drafted from the report excerpt by the LLM pipeline (reverse-bafu draft)
strategy.note: basis: the chromic acid column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000' - i.e. per 3000 kg of anthraquinone; allocation: none stated. Review every derivation; unreviewed entries have reviewed_by = null.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.note: report sha256 68e0839ffea919f9…, text sha256 6d1899c288e051fa…

gaps_reported_by_model: The dataset is an 80/20 average: 'an average process from the chromic acid process in Tab. 44.3 and the information at EMPA from the former studies is established - with an amount of 80% chromic acid process'. Only the chromic acid column is printed; 'the respective information from EMPA is not shown here due to confidentiality reasons'. The extracted list is therefore the 80 % share only.

The EMPA share contributes chlorobenzene (modelled as benzene + chlorine at 95 % yield) and aluminium chloride (modelled as aluminium + chlorine at 95 % yield). No amounts are given, so those four inputs are NOT included here.
The sulphuric acid amount actually used is 'the stoechiometric value based on an efficiency of 95%', which the report does not print.
Electricity, steam, infrastructure and both transports are named by the report but carry no numbers; they are free parameters for calibration.
The air emissions are given as percentage rules applied to inputs the report itself replaces, so their absolute values are uncertain.
'Due to confidentiality reasons, only the cumulated data from this dataset are available for the user of ...' - the dataset's own unit-process table is not published.
skipped_items: air (flow rate): ignore — Explicitly excluded by the report: 'The amount of air consumed is not shown in the ecoinvent dataset according to Frischknecht et al. (2007).' It is also a flow rate, not an amount per batch.

Sulphuric acid to air: no flow chosen (No candidate is airborne sulphuric acid or a sulfate aerosol. Sulfur Dioxide would be a different substance with a different formation route, and mapping sulphuric acid mist onto SO2 would be a substitution the report does not make. Reported as missing instead.)

naphthalene: ignore — Belongs to the naphthalene route, marked only with 'x' (no quantity). The report says 'this second source allows no quantification of the process in three of the four cases' and builds the dataset from the chromic acid column only.
xylene: ignore — Unquantified column of a route not used for this dataset.
butadiene: ignore — Unquantified column of a route not used for this dataset.
anthraquinone: product — Reference product; fixes the basis at 3000 kg.

technosphere.comment: The report explicitly rejects this number: 'As then the above listed amount of sulphuric acid is not sufficient for the process equation, instead the stoechiometric value based on an efficiency of 95% is used here.' provenance.factor_source: g -> kg (x0.001) and then the table basis is 3000 kg of product while this value is printed 'per kg product'; x3000 puts it on the same basis (x3000): net factor 3.0

biosphere.comment: Rule-derived, not printed as a number. Mapped to chromium VI because sodium dichromate is a Cr(VI) salt; low confidence on that mapping.

provenance.quote: and 0.2% of the sodium dichromate input (assumption);
provenance.per: per 3000 kg anthraquinone (the 'chromic acid' column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000')
